answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by pricing identity through a bond partitioned per independent, human-anchored cluster rather than per key. One operator can mint thousands of keys, so weight is bounded by distinct anchors behind them, not headcount. Each spend must clear a small marble of collateral, slashed rather than refunded, if a cluster's members vote alike on a contested task. To farm nectar from reward pools, an attacker must post real value across many anchors. The cost stops being one script and becomes a steep ledge of capital at risk that honest agents never pay.
